field_density.note: 🔴 I FIRST WROTE 'density not queried, a query would be decoration' AND THE VALIDATOR REFUSED IT, CORRECTLY. I had decided a rule did not apply to me because the paper's relevance was not in doubt — but density is not about relevance, it is about where a paper sits in a field, and it costs one request. entries.proposition: 🔴 THE VARIANT IS A VUS, STATED IN THE PAPER'S OWN FIRST SENTENCE OF GENETIC ANALYSIS, AND THE REVIEW THAT CITES THIS CASE DOES NOT SAY SO. PMID 42128308 §9 presents this case as 'a homozygous missense WWOX mutation (p.Ser304Tyr), in which the patient exhibited rapid clinical deterioration and died in early infancy, despite the mutation type typically being associated with milder phenotypes' — offered as one of three counterexamples that falsify the three-class genotype–phenotype framework. The paper classifies the variant ACMG 'unclear clinical significance', twice: here, and in Table 1.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE AUTHORS THEMSELVES SAY THE PATHOGENICITY IS NOT ESTABLISHED, IN THEIR LAST SENTENCE. This is the paper's own conclusion, and it is the sentence the review had to pass over to use the case as a counterexample. A case report that declares its central variant unvalidated cannot, on its own, falsify a genotype–phenotype rule.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE PAPER CANNOT AGREE WITH ITSELF ON THE NUCLEOTIDE, AND ARITHMETIC SETTLES IT AGAINST THE RUNNING TEXT. The Results prose says 'base 991' and writes c.991C>A; Table 1 and the Discussion write c.911C>A. Codon 304 spans nucleotides 910–912, so c.911 falls in codon 304 and c.991 falls in codon 331. Only c.911C>A is consistent with p.Ser304Tyr. THE SAME SENTENCE ALSO GETS THE AMINO ACID WRONG: it reports a change 'from glycine to serine' while the HGVS it prints in the same parenthesis is p.Ser304Tyr, serine to tyrosine. Two errors in one sentence, and the version that propagates into the review is the protein notation, which is the half that is right.
entries.snippet: resulted in a mutation of amino acid 304 from glycine to serine
entries.anchor: Section 2.2 Genetic analysis; compare Table 1 and the Discussion, which both print c.911C>A
entries.found_or_sought: found — I was checking the variant against the review's description and the paper's own two statements of it did not match each other

entries.proposition: 🔴 TABLE 1 PUTS THE ZYGOSITY THE REVIEW USED AND THE CLASSIFICATION IT OMITTED IN THE SAME ROW, AND THIS SNIPPET QUOTES BOTH IN ONE SPAN. c.911C>A (p.Ser304Tyr) — HOMOZYGOTE — developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-28 — AR — from both parents — 'Unclear clinical significance'. So the review's 'homozygous missense' is accurate, and what it drops is four columns to the right of what it kept. The snippet was originally written with the XML markup between the cells and did not verify: the validator strips tags and joins text nodes, so a table locator must quote the ROW AS READ, not the row as marked up. The corrected version is better than the original for the reason the finding exists — the omitted classification is now inside the quoted span rather than asserted to be adjacent to it.

entries.proposition: 🔴 A SECOND CANDIDATE VARIANT IN A SECOND DEE GENE, WHICH THE REVIEW DOES NOT MENTION AT ALL. The child also carries CACNA1A c.4646A>G p.Gln1549Arg, paternal, heterozygous, listed against developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-42 — an AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT condition, so one allele suffices in principle — and also classified 'unclear clinical significance'. The authors argue against its contribution and their argument is reasonable: the DEE-42 phenotype does not match well, and the father carries it without a phenotype. But that is an argument, not a demonstration, and a counterexample used to overturn a genotype–phenotype rule cannot silently drop a competing candidate in a dominant epilepsy gene.

entries.proposition: THE PHENOTYPE ITSELF IS REAL AND SEVERE, AND THIS IS WHAT SURVIVES. Onset at one month; unresponsive glazed eyes with no object tracking; no head control, cannot turn over; bilateral hearing loss with no response to sound; patent foramen ovale; MRI with deepened bilateral frontal sulci, small gyri and a slender corpus callosum; EEG at four months with medium-to-high amplitude spikes and asynchrony between sides. Phenobarbital gave poor control, levetiracetam slight improvement. Consanguineous parents — first cousins — both heterozygous carriers, which is what makes the homozygous state.

AND THE OUTCOME, IN ONE SENTENCE THE PAPER PLACES IN THE FOLLOW-UP SECTION RATHER THAN THE ABSTRACT. Death at six months. The observation stands whatever the variant's formal classification: a child homozygous for a WWOX missense allele, from consanguineous carriers, with a lethal infantile course. What the paper cannot establish is that the missense CAUSED it — which is the step the review takes.

entries.proposition: A GARBLED ATTRIBUTION IN THE THERAPEUTIC PARAGRAPH, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE PARAGRAPH A CLINICIAN WOULD ACT ON. The paper describes the preclinical WWOX gene therapy as using 'an adenoviral vector' — it is adeno-ASSOCIATED, AAV9, a different vector class with different immunogenicity, tropism and regulatory profile — and attributes it to 'the Mahertz and Akhilan laboratories', which are corruptions of Mahzi and Aqeilan. The underlying claim, reduced premature mortality and audiogenic seizure susceptibility with partial normalisation of development, is correct and is PMID 34747138, read on 2026-08-10.
entries.found_or_sought: found — I read the therapeutic paragraph closely because it is the one that names our own corpus, and the vector class was wrong

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE TRIO IS FULLY RESOLVED IN THE PANEL AND ONLY PARTLY IN THE TEXT, AND THE HOMOZYGOSITY IS READ TWICE. Panel F, WWOX: the proband is labelled homozygous on FORWARD and again on REVERSE sequencing — two independent reads of the same base — while father and mother are each labelled heterozygous on forward. Panel G, CACNA1A: proband heterozygous forward and reverse, father heterozygous, MOTHER WILD-TYPE. So the recessive WWOX genotype and the exclusively paternal origin of the CACNA1A allele are both visible as traces, where the running text asserts them and says only that 'Sanger sequencing was used to validate the test results'. This is the strongest evidence in the paper and it is entirely in the figure.

Each trace carries a boxed base and a red arrow at the variant position.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE ADJUDICATION I OPENED THE PANEL FOR FAILED, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. The paper writes c.991C>A in the running text and conclusion and c.911C>A in Table 1 and the discussion. I inspected the traces to settle it. The panel shows the substitution is C→A — the proband's boxed base reads A where both parents read C, against the flanking sequence GCTCTGCAACATCCTTCTC[·]CAACGAGCTGCACCGTCGCC — which is consistent with BOTH candidate positions, because both are C>A. A chromatogram carries no coordinate. So the figure CANNOT resolve the discrepancy, and the only thing that does is arithmetic: codon 304 spans nucleotides 910–912, so c.911 is in codon 304 and c.991 is in codon 331. The panel corroborates the substitution and is silent on the position. Recording a failed adjudication as a failed adjudication is cheaper than leaving a reader to assume the figure settled it.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1 panel F, patient forward trace: sequence above the chromatogram reads G C T C T G C A A C A T C C T T C T C, then the boxed and arrowed base, then C A A C G A G C T G C A C C G T C G C C. Proband boxed base A; father and mother boxed base C at the same position with identical flanking sequence. No nucleotide coordinate appears anywhere in the panel; the numeric scale above each trace is the read position, running 140–170 for the patient forward trace and 250–280 for the reverse.
entries.anchor: Figure 1, panel F, patient forward and reverse traces against the parental traces
entries.found_or_sought: sought, and the answer was no — I went to the panel to settle c.911 against c.991 and a chromatogram cannot carry a coordinate

entries.proposition: THE IMAGING PANELS, AND WHERE I STOP. Panels A–C are axial sections with red arrows to the frontal lobe (A, B) and to the 'temporale lobe' (C, sic); panel D is a sagittal section with an arrow to a visibly slender corpus callosum, which is the finding the caption claims and the one an inspection can support. Panel E is a 16-channel EEG epoch, Fp1 to T6. 🔴 I DECLINE TO ADJUDICATE THE EEG. The caption claims spikes 'primarily observed in the bilateral frontal Poles and frontal and central regions during sleep' with occasional spread to occipital areas; a single representative epoch cannot establish a regional distribution, and reading one from a reproduction is exactly the cross-figure over-reach that failed three times on 2026-08-10. The epoch is consistent with the caption and does not verify it.

verbatim_locators.figure_provenance_note: 🔴 THE FIGURE ROUTE IS A FINDING IN ITSELF. PMC's bin path 404s for both the figure and the supplementary; the PMC OA package is offered only over ftp://; the Frontiers HTML serves image_m at 1056x604. The publisher PDF holds the same figure at 1955x1118, 300 effective ppi, DeviceRGB, smask = 0 — 1.85x more pixels per dimension than the served copy. Measured before extracting, per the rule corrected this evening: smask == 0 means the extracted stream is what the page shows, so extraction is faithful here and the digest is of the publisher's bytes. Reading a Sanger base call from the served copy would have been reading it with a third of the pixels the publisher shipped.
